# Gauntlet Loop 5.2.0 release review

25 September 2026. The [upgrade run](../gauntlet/v52-reconsideration-2026-09-25/progress.md) is governed by 5.1.0, against eight checks frozen before source edits. The outgoing nine-file package and release evidence are preserved under [versions](../versions/README.md). No benchmark was run.

## Change and purpose

When feedback challenges the problem interpretation, reconsider before making more affected edits, even if existing checks pass. Ordinary defects still receive ordinary fixes. Independent interpretations and concrete scenarios help expose competing readings; agreement cannot redefine the user's goal. Settled choices proceed, while consequential unresolved preferences get concrete alternatives and a recommendation.

Incoming questions and additions preserve unfinished objectives. Stops and invalidating corrections reach affected workers; delayed results are checked against current requirements. Reconsideration spends the existing allowance and preserves review lineage. Discussion does not replace independent acceptance. These rules live in the skill, existing references, portable template and worked examples; no separate orchestration framework is required.

## Review findings and repairs

Three fresh independent Opus 5.5 reviews first found missing portable stop/choice semantics, then a timing regression introduced by compression. Both were corrected. The third review accepts source-level C1–C6; [exact findings and identities](../gauntlet/v52-reconsideration-2026-09-25/evidence/reviews/round-3.json) remain inspectable. An advisory concern about optional software checks was settled by direct source inspection in the acceptance lane; the fresh Claude reviewer did not inspect that reference.

Eight initial simulated next-action responses exposed three material failures: demanding a plan fail a new test before feasibility was known, reporting planned cancellation as already completed, and weakening a stated attendance trade-off. Four targeted reruns corrected these failures. One still discouraged repeat attendance more strongly than the supplied objective warranted; several exceeded the requested response length. These are limitations, not silently excluded successes.

The initial standalone drafting attempt timed out. A later self-contained task returned a prompt, but independent review found omitted continuity and reconsideration semantics. Its source snapshot predates the final timing correction. One feedback-guided repair returned a 643-word prompt and received scoped ACCEPT in [integration review 4](../gauntlet/v52-reconsideration-2026-09-25/evidence/reviews/round-4.json). The [scenario index](../gauntlet/v52-reconsideration-2026-09-25/evidence/scenarios/index.json) preserves the failed original and repair separately. The repair received specific corrective instructions; no clean forward generation from the final source bytes exists, and the generated prompt was not executed.

## Verification and boundaries

Package, ZIP and portable identities, archive bytes, local links, YAML/frontmatter and generated research indexes are checked in the run's final evidence. The existing offline suite ran 182 tests with one skip and no failures. Its earlier receipt was reconstructed from a tool result; the final [test receipt](../gauntlet/v52-reconsideration-2026-09-25/evidence/tests.json) records the requested rerun with code/package/test input identities and actual output. The archive counts distinguish 34 original skill files (25 older plus nine outgoing) from 37 verifier entries, which also include the archived release review, manifest and previous checksum list. The entrypoint and portable file remain within 16,000 and 110,000 bytes; the limits were not raised. The package validator checks presence of the two new carrier markers from version 5.2 onward; marker presence is not semantic or behavioral proof.

Known delegated model usage is **$5.260492**, including the final review. Unsuccessful attempts and unknown costs are reported in the run. CLI amounts are API-equivalent usage, not subscription cash or full research cost. Two early timeouts have unknown usage; preparation, lead and human time are also unknown. The dollar guard is soft.

Two [reported live pilots](../gauntlet/v52-reconsideration-2026-09-25/evidence/pilot-observations.json) described useful changes and positive reactions to concepts; `independently_reproduced_here` is false. Failures included omitted image filenames breaking three handoffs, a worker over-generalizing one group's capacity, and two concurrent timeouts with unknown cost. Responses to later design synthesis were still unknown at the evidence cutoff. Their costs remain separate, source material stays private, and no controlled comparison identifies the cause of satisfaction. This release does not establish fewer corrections, faster delivery, automatic learning or native host scheduling enforcement. The private installed customization and active pilots were not overwritten.

## Remaining issues

- The pre-existing drafting placeholder permits `features enabled or none`, although the full contract always includes `evidence_ladder`. The generated record is checked explicitly; a future source cleanup must reconcile the whole vocabulary rather than silently change old evidence.
- Word pressure can remove required semantics from generated prompts despite correct source instructions. The actual generated prompt must be inspected; this package is not an enforcement boundary.
- Compacting duplicated entrypoint material relies on reference loading. The review checked that acceptance, budgets and resume obligations remain, but did not measure comprehension or retrieval cost.

Release disposition and precise acceptance evidence are in the [run state](../gauntlet/v52-reconsideration-2026-09-25/state.yaml).
